exposure: clinical form of jaundice (neonatal, prolonged, hemolytic disease of the newborn)
bilirubin measurement method (total serum bilirubin, transcutaneous bilirubin)
outcome: prevalence of different clinical forms of jaundice (NJ, PJN, HDN)
cohort: The study participants were 616 infants diagnosed with various clinical forms of neonatal jaundice (NJ, PJN, HDN) who received inpatient medical care at a Children's Clinical Hospital in Kyiv between 2017 and 2021.
finding: The study showed a decrease in hospitalizations for infant jaundice from 2017 to 2021, with prolonged jaundice being the most prevalent form, and a history of cesarean section was associated with prolonged jaundice.
mod_finding: A history of cesarean section was associated with the manifestation of prolonged jaundice (PJN).
